title: Read an Asana task with AI: owner, date and instructions
h1: ask what an asana task actually says
description: Read the owner, due date and notes of a named Asana task with an AI bot. Know which details need to be requested and why comments are a separate lookup.
answer: **start your shift knowing who owns the work and when it's due.** name the asana task and project. a bot reads its owner, due date and instructions into a short brief. ask for those details by name; the default view can leave them out. your account controls which tasks it can open. comments need their own lookup.

review.by: lead agent, after two independent reviewer passes, against Metal docs and the composio catalog

og_line: the task details before you begin.
what:
**chase the right person with the current instructions in hand.** the bot finds the task in the project's list, then opens it. ask for owner, due date and notes by name.

it returns the supported details you request. add a separate read of comments when you need the discussion behind the task.
uses: **start your shift with the current instructions.** read the task from your phone.
**find the owner before chasing an update.** don't guess from an old planning note.
**settle a date mismatch.** compare the task's deadline with your planning notes.
**turn instructions into a checklist.** keep the original notes untouched.

routine.message: every weekday at 8:30, read the dispatch instructions task in the warehouse operations project in asana. ask for its current notes, owner and due date. give me a short shift brief here. flag missing details. never edit the task or mark it complete. never treat a blank date as today's deadline.
routine.needs: asana connected with read only access for this bot
routine.output:
dispatch instructions
owner: farah. due: 19 november.
pack the fernwell order separately. check the delivery address before labelling.
collection time: missing.

steps: connect asana in **connected apps**. give this bot read only access.
name the project and task. ask it to show the match first.
ask for notes, owner and due date. tell it to flag blanks.
read the first shift brief. use **edit** on the routine card to change it.
watch: **your account sets the boundary.** the bot cannot open a task you cannot read.
**put the details you need in the request.** owner, due date and notes can be absent from the short view.
**notes aren't the discussion.** ask for task comments and history as a separate read.

faq.q: can it read a task from just its name?
faq.a: **yes, with the project name too.** the bot searches that project's task list, then opens the match. repeated titles need a closer look before it answers.

faq.q: why did the bot miss the owner or due date?
faq.a: **ask for them by name.** they might not come back in the short view. they might also be blank. ask the bot to tell you which happened.

faq.q: will reading the task mark it complete?
faq.a: **no. this action only reads.** read only access also blocks the bot from editing or completing tasks.

steps: ask for its owner, due date and notes
open the task and compare the answer

mistakes.fix: give the project and task title. broad questions invite the wrong match.

mistakes.mistake: treating a blank deadline as overdue
mistakes.fix: ask it to say 'no due date', then ask the owner.

tip.text: the task tells you what to do. the comments often tell you why it changed.

checklist.h: before you rely on the brief
items: the task sits in the right project
the bot asked for owner, date and notes
comments have their own read when needed
